clue.text: Discourage Secretary-General, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to sap their courage or nerve
the Secretary-General of the United Nations is, read whimsically

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the word into UN MAN: the head of the United Nations is one example of such a person, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: To unman is to deprive of courage, which is what discouraging someone does.

clue.text: Cover is wonderful, though not at first including composer

indicators.note: including means the composer goes inside
not at first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: super means wonderful
Gustav Holst was an English composer, of The Planets

explanation.surface: A remark that a cover is splendid, albeit not initially, with a composer involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not at first' removes the opening letter; 'including' wraps the remainder round the composer's name. 'Cover' is the verb, as with furniture fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: To upholster is to cover furniture with padding and fabric.

clue.text: Saw a gun

definitions.meaning: a saw is an old saying or proverb
an early machine gun named after its inventor

explanation.definitionFit: A maxim is a pithy saying, like a saw, and the Maxim was a famous machine gun.

clue.text: Give a mention, in a way

definitions.text: Give a mention, in a way

indicators.note: in a way means the letters are arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Putting someone forward is one way of mentioning them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' rearranges A MENTION; the whole clue also describes what the answer does.
explanation.definitionFit: To nominate someone is to put their name forward, a kind of mention.

clue.text: "It was enough to make any man sick," as Pepys said, wrongly

definitions.text: It was enough to make any man sick

indicators.note: said wrongly means the letters of these two words are set out in a wrong order

explanation.surface: A quotation from the famous diarist Samuel Pepys complaining that something turned his stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges PEPYS and SAID together. Samuel Pepys was a seventeenth-century English diarist, which makes the quotation plausible; the definition describes what upsets the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigestion is a stomach upset, the kind of ailment that would make anyone feel sick.

clue.text: To use dendrochronology you need a tree

definitions.meaning: dendrochronology is dating wood by its tree rings

explanation.walkthrough: Dendrochronology is the science of dating timber by counting annual growth rings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tree-ring science establishes the age of timber, and the date palm is a tree.

clue.text: Tapestries woven for entertainment

indicators.note: woven means the letters are interlaced into a new order

explanation.surface: Wall hangings produced to amuse visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woven' suits tapestries but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A striptease is a form of entertainment in which a performer undresses.

clue.text: Closing down racket in England

indicators.note: the racket goes in the other piece

parts.note: din means racket or noise

explanation.surface: A noisy place in England being shut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' is noise, not a sports bat.
explanation.definitionFit: An ending is a finish or closing, as when a business closes down.

clue.text: Swinging tune: is rag time indicated by this?

indicators.note: a swinging tune moves about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A jazz musician asks how ragtime's rhythm is shown on the score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swinging' rearranges TUNE, IS and RAG. In music, a time signature at the start of the stave shows the beats per bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A time signature is the musical notation that tells a player the metre of a piece.

clue.text: Allotment has two areas

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area
a ward is an area, as of a city or hospital

explanation.surface: A garden plot covering two areas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two areas' gives two pieces: A, the abbreviation, and WARD, an electoral area.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is something allotted or granted, as in a legal settlement.

clue.text: Test going in mostly straight line

indicators.note: the test is placed going in, that is inside, the other piece
mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: hetero is slang for straight, meaning heterosexual
an exam is a test

explanation.surface: An instruction about an examination that sticks to a straight line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the final letter; 'going in' places the test within the trimmed word. 'straight' tempts as the definition, but the line is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hexameter is a line of verse with six metrical feet, as in classical epic poetry.

clue.text: Follow the master's teaching

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
MA is a Master of Arts degree, abbreviated

explanation.surface: A disciple urged to follow what the master teaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the master's' points to the Master of Arts, MA, rather than a teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a set of doctrines laid down and taught as authoritative.

clue.text: Keen officer provides accommodation for a number of soldiers

indicators.note: the officer houses the other letters, so they go inside

parts.note: LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer
men is the usual word for a body of soldiers in the ranks

explanation.surface: An eager officer finds billets for a group of troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like an adjective meaning eager; here it is the verb to wail for the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to wail in mourning, so it is a synonym for lamenting aloud.

clue.text: European resort -about to empty

parts.note: a spa is a resort town

indicators.note: about means the word that follows is turned round

parts.note: to drain is to empty

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker at a European resort is about to leave it deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the verb round, giving NIARD; the clue's dash in some printings is just punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spaniard is a native of Spain, a European country, so he is a European.

clue.text: Parachute jump carries soldiers into widespread conflict

indicators.note: carries means the soldiers are inside the jump

parts.note: a free fall is the part of a parachute jump before the canopy opens
OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A parachute drop takes troops into a large-scale war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' places the soldiers inside the jump, splitting it after its fourth letter. OR, Other Ranks, is a standard abbreviation for soldiers not commissioned.
explanation.definitionFit: A free-for-all is a disorganised fight in which everyone joins in.

clue.text: Presumably Dr. Dolittle could have a frank discussion

definitions.meaning: Doctor Dolittle, the fictional vet, could talk with animals, a turkey included
an idiom meaning to speak plainly about business

explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Dolittle is the children's-book doctor who talks to animals, so he could literally chat with a turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to discuss something plainly and get down to business.

clue.text: Bally enthusiastically?

definitions.meaning: read as ball-y, like a ball, and a shot is a cannonball
an idiom for immediately and eagerly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bally' is old British slang for 'bloody', but here it is split as BALL plus -Y, meaning like a ball, and a shot can be a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means very quickly and willingly, without hesitation.

clue.text: Somewhere to sleep? Nonsense!

definitions.meaning: short for bunkum, meaning rubbish or claptrap

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a narrow bed and nonsense, short for bunkum.

clue.text: Where you could have seen first-time flier Jack cry

definitions.text: Where you could have seen first-time flier

parts.note: the jackpot or pool of money is the kitty
to hawk is to cry wares for sale

explanation.surface: A place where you might have spotted Jack shouting on his first flight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wright brothers made the first powered flight at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, in 1903.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, is where the Wright brothers made the first powered aeroplane flight.

clue.text: I'll get confused with erratic standards

indicators.note: get confused means the letters are jumbled together

parts.note: the first person I, whose 'll is will

explanation.surface: Someone muddles their principles with erratic ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get confused' rearranges I and ERRATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Criteria are standards by which things are judged.

clue.text: Search a string of railway wagons

definitions.meaning: to ... through something is to search it thoroughly
a railway term for a set of coaches or wagons coupled together

explanation.definitionFit: Raking means searching thoroughly, and a rake is the railway term for a coupled set of carriages.

clue.text: Legendary creature, exhausted, swallows something to give relief

indicators.note: the exhausted piece swallows the other, so it goes inside

parts.note: spent means exhausted
an easer is something that eases, giving relief

explanation.surface: A mythical beast, worn out, gulps down a remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallows' places the reliever inside the word for exhausted, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea serpent is a monster of sailors' legend, a classic mythical creature.

clue.text: Make rough drawing of small vessel after beginning on seascape

indicators.note: after means the vessel comes after the letter
the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a ketch is a small two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: An artist sketches a little boat while starting a seascape.
explanation.walkthrough: S comes from the start of 'seascape'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a quick preliminary drawing, so producing one is drafting a picture roughly as a plain synonym.

clue.text: Combination of drugs can make you crazy

parts.note: crack is a form of cocaine
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A warning that mixing drugs can drive you mad.
explanation.walkthrough: Two slang drug names, crack and pot, combine to make the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot is an eccentric or crazy person; here used adjectivally for crazy schemes or ideas.

clue.text: A spell in the French army

annotationWithheld.why: A spell in the French army (5): CHARM is 'a spell', but no parse found for 'in the French army' giving CHARM letters; scan reads the same
annotationWithheld.clue: A spell in the French army

clue.text: Squat, or plump on top of sofa

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it
the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: tubby means plump

explanation.surface: Someone short and stout, or flopping down on the top of a sofa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squat' and 'plump' look like verbs about sitting down, but both are adjectives here.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubby means short and thick, the same as squat in shape.

clue.text: Light wood — pick up a plank

indicators.note: in a down clue, pick up means read upwards, reversed

parts.note: a slab is a flat piece, a plank

explanation.surface: Choosing a plank of light timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pick up' turns A SLAB round, upwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very lightweight timber used in models.

clue.text: Look here! Island's got left out

indicators.note: left out means the letter is removed

parts.note: Islay is a Scottish island

explanation.surface: An exclamation that an island has been forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: Islay is a Hebridean island off Scotland's west coast, known for whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: I say is an exclamation to attract attention, like 'Look here!'.

clue.text: Plate that's large when heated

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
het is a dialect past form of heat, as in het up

explanation.surface: A dish that seems to grow when it gets hot.
explanation.walkthrough: HET is the old dialect form surviving in 'het up'. An ashet is a Scottish and northern English word for a large serving dish.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland and the north of England, an ashet is a large oval serving dish or platter.

clue.text: Country investing a lot upfront in another

indicators.note: investing means putting money in, so the letters are put into the other country

parts.note: Austria is another country

indicators.note: upfront means only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: One nation pours a lot of money into another as up-front investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upfront' takes just the first letter of 'lot'; 'investing' puts the A and that L into the other country before its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia is a country, indeed a whole continent.

clue.text: Harmonise and produce music in competition

parts.note: to match is to go together or harmonise
to play is to produce music

explanation.surface: Musicians harmonise and perform in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical surface hides a golf term: match play is scored by holes won rather than total strokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Match play is a form of golf competition scored by the number of holes won.

clue.text: There's something wanting here, I'm sorry to say

parts.note: a stands for one thing, something
a lack is something wanting or missing

explanation.surface: A regretful admission that something is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'something wanting' as A LACK.
explanation.definitionFit: Alack is an archaic exclamation of regret or sorrow, like alas.
